audit.report: A replayable batch job (batch_replayable_inventory, pid 341560) held a transaction open for 4.1 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 55-77% against a 95% SLO. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting, but trade-off analysis showed the job had ~896 seconds remaining, which would cost ~$199,188 in lost checkout revenue and exceed the 60-second degradation tolerance. Both guardians agreed to terminate the batch job, which has a 4-minute replay cost and an interruptible policy. The executor terminated the session, and the verifier confirmed full recovery: zero lock waits, 100% checkout success over 10 seconds, and no protected settlements affected. Total negotiation and recovery took 54.9 seconds in a single round.
audit.root_cause: A long-running replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile) held an idle-in-transaction lock that blocked checkout sessions, causing SLO breach.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory: add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout to prevent idle transactions from holding locks beyond a safe threshold (e.g., 30s).
For batch_replayable_inventory: ensure the job checkpoints more frequently than every 900s so replay cost stays well below the 60s business degradation budget.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian efficiently pivoted from wait to terminate after evidence probes quantified the trade-off; the Continuity Guardian accepted immediately with no objection. No rounds were wasted and no invariants were violated.
follow_ups: Implement idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_worker role to auto-abort stalled transactions.
Instrument batch_replayable_inventory to emit progress heartbeats so remaining runtime is observable without manual probes.
Add batch_replayable_inventory to the change_calendar with its nightly window documented.
